findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: The new fetch and delete tracing calls unconditionally use Error, even when no error occurred or no rows need cleaning. The same happens in count-based cleanup and orphaned-tag cleanup, so healthy cleanup runs now generate error-level records, potentially triggering false alerts and dumping large ID lists into normal production logs. These traces should use Debug; Error should be reserved for actual failures.

findings.title: Large cleanup batches exceed PostgreSQL's parameter limit
findings.body: The new DELETE binds one parameter per selected ID, but only SQLite receives parameter-limit handling. PostgreSQL accepts at most 65,535 bind parameters, so a sufficiently large backlog with cleanupjob_batchsize above that limit makes every delete fail and prevents retention cleanup from progressing. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not have this restriction. Cap or split the deletion batches according to the database's parameter limit.

findings.title: SQLite ID-list construction performs quadratic copying
findings.body: Each iteration formats the entire accumulated ID string into a new string, making SQL construction quadratic in the number of IDs. A batch containing tens of thousands of IDs, explicitly supported by the new test, creates gigabytes of transient allocations just to construct a DELETE statement. This adds substantial CPU and GC overhead to cleanup. Build the list with a strings.Builder or an append-based byte buffer instead.

findings.title: The shortened ticker increases load from every cleanup job
findings.body: Changing the shared ticker from ten minutes to one minute also runs snapshot, dashboard-version, image, invitation, short-URL, and query-history cleanup ten times as often. Each pass still has a nine-minute timeout; if a pass takes longer than one minute, a buffered tick causes the next pass to start immediately, potentially keeping these database maintenance jobs running continuously. Preserve the existing shared interval rather than changing all cleanup jobs as part of the annotation SQL fix.
